title: The Oceans: Relief, Salinity, and Temperature

questions.question: A narrow stretch of water joining two larger bodies, like the Palk Strait, is a:
questions.rationale: A strait is narrow water between landmasses; an isthmus is the opposite — narrow land joining two larger landmasses, like Panama.

questions.question: The continental shelf typically extends down to a depth of about:
questions.rationale: The shelf — under a tenth of the ocean floor — reaches about 200 m and hosts the richest fisheries and offshore oilfields.

questions.question: The world's longest mountain chain is:
questions.rationale: The mid-ocean ridge system runs about 65,000 km along diverging plate boundaries, far out-stretching any land range.

questions.question: The deepest point of the world ocean, about 11 km down, lies in the:
questions.rationale: The Challenger Deep of the Mariana Trench reaches about 11 km — deep enough to submerge Mount Everest with over 2 km to spare.

questions.question: The average salinity of the world ocean is about:
questions.rationale: Average ocean salinity is about 35 grams of salt per kilogram of water — 35 practical salinity units.

questions.question: The Baltic Sea's unusually low salinity (about 7–10) is caused mainly by:
options: Dilution by river influx and low evaporation
questions.rationale: Rivers pour freshwater into the Baltic faster than the cool, weakly evaporating sea can concentrate salt.

questions.question: Which water body is hypersaline, at roughly 330?
questions.rationale: The land-locked Dead Sea, with no outlet and intense evaporation, reaches about 330 — dense enough to float swimmers.

questions.question: Salinity is generally highest at which latitudes?
questions.rationale: Near 20–30° N and S, evaporation outruns rainfall, maximising salinity; the equator is slightly diluted by heavy rain.

questions.question: The ocean layer in which temperature drops fastest with depth is the:
questions.rationale: The thermocline is the divider between the warm wind-stirred surface lid and the cold, stable deep water.

questions.question: Coastal places enjoy mild climates compared with the interior chiefly because:
options: Water heats and cools slowly due to high heat capacity
questions.rationale: Ocean water's high heat capacity damps temperature swings, so the sea warms coasts in winter and cools them in summer.
